title: Collaborative practice regulations defined and limited by statute
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B3/4 requires the board of registration in medicine and the board of registration in pharmacy to issue rules and regulations to implement collaborative drug therapy management pursuant to section 24B1/2 and sections 7 and 9 of chapter 94C, and provides that the rules and regulations shall govern each collaborative practice agreement and shall be defined and limited by section 24B1/2, chapter 94C and other applicable statutes. Among the issues the boards shall address is the scope of conditions or diseases to be managed, the initial list of which shall not include more than 5 disease states, the 5 diseases selected for the retail setting to be from among those referenced in clause (5) of subsection (c) of section 24B1/2. The boards shall reconsider the regulations on a periodic basis, as considered appropriate by the commissioner, for the purposes of adding or removing disease states and of updating the rules and regulations as necessary.
exam_relevance: Tests that the collaborative practice regulations govern each agreement but are, in the statute's own words, defined and limited by section 24B1/2 and chapter 94C.

numeric_facts.fact: Maximum number of disease states on the initial list
numeric_facts.conditions: initial list; for the retail setting, drawn from those referenced in s. 24B1/2(c)(5)

common_confusions: Section 24B3/4 says the regulations shall govern each agreement and shall be defined and limited by section 24B1/2; it does not itself say how a regulation worded differently from the statute is to be read.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B3/4 on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-17.
